findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler remains abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler, which defines several abstract methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data). The class body is just `pass` and does not implement any of these methods. As a result, the class itself is abstract and attempting to instantiate it will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`. Since MetricAlertFire sets `detector_handler = MetricAlertDetectorHandler`, any Detector with type 'metric_alert_fire' will crash in `Detector.detector_handler` when `group_type.detector_handler(self)` is called. This will break the workflow engine for that detector type.

findings.title: Test builds expected occurrence with wrong group key, causing assertion failure
findings.body: In TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe, the expected_result is constructed with an IssueOccurrence built using group_key "val1" (via build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", ...)), but evaluate_group_key_value is invoked with group_key "group_key". The handler's build_occurrence_and_event_data hook will produce an occurrence whose fingerprint is based on "group_key", so the actual result's occurrence fingerprint differs from the expected one. IssueOccurrence is a dataclass and equality includes all fields, so the assertion `handler.evaluate_group_key_value(...) == expected_result` will fail. The expected occurrence should be built with the same group_key ("group_key") as used in the evaluation.
